e: Create an IAM policy that grants only the permissions each department needs and attach it to the IAM groups, so every user added to a group inherits least-privilege access. Roles can't be attached to groups, SCPs don't grant permissions, and a permissions boundary only sets a maximum.

The existing statement puts s3:DeleteObject on the bucket ARN, but object actions apply to object ARNs (bucket-name/*), so deletes fail. Adding a statement allowing only s3:DeleteObject on arn:aws:s3:::bucket-name/* fixes it with least privilege. s3:*Object and s3:* are broader than needed, and the pattern bucket-name* is malformed.

S3 Object Lock with a retention period (on a versioned bucket) prevents modification or deletion until the date, static website hosting with a bucket policy allowing public read serves the files, so the data is publicly readable yet immutable. IAM permissions or Lambda restoration can't enforce immutability.

AWS CloudFormation lets you define the validated infrastructure as a template (Auto Scaling group, ALB, RDS) and deploy it repeatedly for development and production across two AZs in an automated way. Systems Manager, Config, and Elastic Beanstalk don't replicate arbitrary existing infrastructure.

A VPC endpoint (gateway endpoint for S3) lets the EC2 instances reach S3 over the AWS private network without traversing the public internet. KMS handles encryption, and private subnets or virtual private gateways don't provide private connectivity to S3.

Write-through caching updates the cache whenever data is written to the database, so the cache always matches the database. Lazy loading can return stale data, and TTL only expires entries; AppConfig isn't a caching strategy.

For a one-time 100 GB transfer over a 100 Mbps link (a few hours), the AWS CLI s3 sync command uses HTTPS (encrypted in transit) and needs no agents or devices, so it has the least operational overhead. DataSync requires deploying an agent, Snowball is overkill, and VPN setup adds work.

ECS on Fargate supports Windows containers, and a scheduled task (EventBridge schedule) runs the container every 10 minutes and bills only for the 1 to 3 minutes of runtime. Lambda doesn't support Windows container images, and Windows Task Scheduler inside a standalone task isn't the way to schedule it.

Use AWS Organizations (all features) to create and manage the multiple accounts, and set up IAM Identity Center integrated with the corporate directory for centralized authentication and access to all the accounts. Cognito or direct Directory Service integration in Organizations isn't how access is centralized.

S3 Glacier with Expedited retrievals returns data in typically 1 to 5 minutes, meeting the 5-minute requirement at lower storage cost than Standard-IA/One Zone-IA for rarely used archives. Standard retrievals take hours.

S3 hosts the static website cheaply, ECS with Fargate runs the containers without managing servers (simplest deployment and lower operations), and a managed RDS cluster provides the relational database. CloudFront isn't a host, and EKS or EC2-based compute adds management.

EFS is a scalable, highly available NFS file system with no minimum size that multiple Linux instances can mount, including from on premises over VPN or Direct Connect using the mount targets in each AZ. EBS Multi-Attach is block storage limited to one AZ, and FSx options don't match all requirements.

An SCP attached to the root OU that denies access to billing actions applies to all member accounts, including their root users (SCPs affect even the root user of member accounts). IAM identity-based policies can't restrict the root user, and converting to consolidated billing removes governance features.

An SNS dead-letter queue (an SQS queue) captures messages that couldn't be delivered to the HTTPS endpoint, and an SQS retention period up to 14 days lets the team analyze them, with no development. SNS DLQ targets must be SQS queues, not Kinesis or DynamoDB.

With point-in-time recovery enabled, DynamoDB can export table data to S3 from the continuous backups without consuming read capacity or affecting availability, with no code. EMR, Streams plus Lambda, or scheduled Lambda scans use RCUs or need coding.

Standard SQS queues guarantee at-least-once delivery and cost less than FIFO, which is enough because requests only need to be processed at least once. SSE-KMS encrypts messages, and the Lambda execution role needs kms:Decrypt (the role, not the function, holds permissions).

Organizing the accounts into OUs and attaching an SCP that restricts which EC2 instance types can be launched centrally prevents oversized instances with little effort. Systems Manager templates, Service Catalog, or EventBridge with Lambda need more development or don't strictly prevent creation.

Amazon Transcribe converts call audio in many languages to text, Amazon Translate translates the text to English (and supports new languages), and Amazon Comprehend produces the sentiment analysis, all managed with no ML model maintenance. Comprehend doesn't translate audio, Polly is text to speech, and Lex builds chatbots.

The policy allows TerminateInstances but also denies it when the source IP is not in 192.0.2.0/24 or 203.0.113.0/24 (NotIpAddress). An explicit deny wins, so the request was denied because it didn't originate from those CIDR blocks.

Amazon Macie runs sensitive data discovery jobs on S3 using managed data identifiers to find PII and financial data such as passport and credit card numbers. Audit Manager, S3 Inventory with Athena, and S3 Select can't detect sensitive data types.

A Storage Gateway file gateway replaces the NFS storage with local caching and S3 backing, and a volume gateway (cached volumes) replaces block storage using iSCSI with local caching, without re-architecting applications. S3 can't be mounted natively, and EFS isn't designed with local caching for on-premises servers.

A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 routes S3 traffic privately within the Region and has no hourly or data processing charge, which eliminates NAT gateway data processing costs. NAT instances or additional NAT gateways still cost money.

An S3 Lifecycle rule that expires noncurrent versions while keeping only the two most recent (NewerNoncurrentVersions) deletes older versions automatically with no operational work. Lambda or Batch Operations need maintenance, and disabling versioning doesn't retain versions.

Hosted connections from an AWS Direct Connect Partner are available at lower speeds such as 200 Mbps, which is much cheaper than a dedicated 1 Gbps port and sufficient for under 10% utilization, while remaining private and secure. Dedicated connections are only 1, 10, or 100 Gbps, and sharing doesn't cut cost for this account.

DataSync preserves Windows file permissions (NTFS ACLs/metadata) when copying from SMB file servers to FSx for Windows, using an on-premises agent or one running on a Snowcone for offline-friendly transfer. Copying through S3 or CLI loses the file permission metadata.
